key_factors: (a)(3) tariff shift to subheading 8473.30
decisive_step: Soldering and oven brazing assembly of the heat sink components in Mexico

key_factors: (a)(3) tariff shift or (b)(1) essential character of the Canadian panel assembly
decisive_step: Manufacturing the MDF/acrylic panels and affixing the vinyl skin in Canada

Under 19 CFR 102.11(a)(3) or 102.11(b)(1), the production of the structural panel components and application of the vinyl skin in Canadaeither satisfies the applicable tariff shift in 19 CFR 102.20 or imparts the essential character to the unassembled rack, conferring Canadian origin.

key_factors: (a)(3) tariff shift to 8421.29

key_factors: (b)(1) essential character of the aluminum alloy sheet

Under 102.11(b)(1), the Chinese aluminum sheet imparts the essential character (consistent with N316637 and N316780), making China the origin.

key_factors: (a)(3) tariff shift to 2106.90
decisive_step: Mixing, formulating, and bottling the cane sugar, maple syrups, water, salt, and natural flavoring into pancake and waffle syrup in Canada.

Consistent with N320159 and N326397, origin is conferred by Canada under 19 CFR 102.11(a)(3).

key_factors: (a)(3) tariff shift to 8541.43
decisive_step: Assembly of photovoltaic cells and other components into finished solar panels in Mexico
flip: If the solar panels were imported prior to the 2022 HTSUS split of subheading 8541.40 (when cells and modules shared a subheading), or if a complete panel (8541.43) were imported into Mexico for minor processing, origin would remain with the country of the solar cells under 102.11(b).
reasoning: The finished solar panels are classified in subheading 8541.43, HTSUS, while the foreign photovoltaic cells are classified in subheading 8541.42, HTSUS. key_factors: (b) essential character of the cereal flakes

reasoning: The Apple Strawberry Oat & Almond Cereal is classified in heading 1904. The 19 CFR 102.20 tariff shift rule for heading 1904 requires a change from any other heading. key_factors: (d)(3) last country where the good underwent production
decisive_step: Final assembly of the manual rack and pinion gear components in Mexico

Moving to 102.11(b), no single non-shifting component from one country imparts the essential character of the entire steering gear assembly. Under 102.11(d)(3), origin is conferred by the last country of production, Mexico.

key_factors: (b) essential character of the LDPE drip lines
decisive_step: Manufacturing of the perforated LDPE drip lines in the United States

Under 102.11(b)(1) and 102.18(b), the single non-shifting material (or the one imparting essential character) determines origin: United States.

key_factors: (b) essential character of the aluminum Cover Casting and Main Board Casting
decisive_step: Casting and forming of the aluminum cover and main board castings in South Korea

Under 102.11(b), the South Korean castings impart the essential character.

key_factors: (a)(3) tariff shift to 3824.99
decisive_step: Mixing and blending of foreign chemical and mineral ingredients in Canada to produce the finished chemical preparation of subheading 3824.99
flip: If one of the foreign inputs were already classified in subheading 3824.99, the tariff shift would fail and origin would be determined under 102.11(b) or (c).
reasoning: Lubrigel L is a formulated chemical preparation used in oilfield drilling operations, classified under subheading 3824.99, HTSUS. Because all foreign inputs (classified in chapters 13, 27, 34, 39, and 68) undergo the required tariff shift during blending in Canada, Canada is the country of origin under 19 CFR 102.11(a)(3).

key_factors: (d)(3) last country where the good underwent production (after (a)(3) and (b)(1) fail to yield a single country)
decisive_step: Macerating neutral grain alcohol with juniper and botanicals, distilling into gin, diluting, and bottling in Canada

key_factors: (a)(3) tariff shift to Chapter 16
decisive_step: Wrapping the frozen scallop medallions in raw bacon in Canada

key_factors: (b) essential character of the plywood substrate

key_factors: (a)(3) tariff shift to heading 7610
decisive_step: Extrusion, cutting, welding, and fabrication of the Turkish aluminum billets and U.S. fabric into an aluminum structure in Canada

key_factors: (b) essential character of the inner and outer rings with gear teeth
decisive_step: Machining and gear-cutting of the inner and outer races/rings in China

key_factors: (a)(3) tariff shift to 8443.31 or 8443.32
decisive_step: Manufacturing the PCBA, imaging unit, developing unit, and toner cartridge in Mexico and assembling them with the Chinese printer transport into the finished printer in Mexico
flip: If the imaging unit, developing unit, and toner cartridge were pre-assembled into the printer transport in China (as in H304677), the transport would be classified as an incomplete printer under GRI 2(a), failing the tariff shift and making China the country of origin.

key_factors: (a)(3) tariff shift to heading 7326
decisive_step: Slitting, stamping, perforating, and forming the stainless steel into bands and housings, and assembling the hose clamps in Canada

key_factors: (b) essential character of the polyethylene film

key_factors: (a)(3) tariff shift to heading 7610
decisive_step: Extrusion, cutting, tapping, welding, and powder coating of Turkish aluminum billets into structural framework components in Canada
flip: Import pre-extruded and fabricated aluminum structural beams and posts from Turkey into Canada solely for packaging with fasteners, preventing the tariff shift in Canada.

key_factors: (a)(3) tariff shift to 3206.11
decisive_step: Surface treatment of titanium dioxide (2823.00) in Canada to produce titanium dioxide pigment (3206.11)
flip: If the titanium dioxide imported from China were already surface-treated or mixed with other substances prior to export to Canada, it would already be classified in subheading 3206.11 and fail the tariff shift in Canada, shifting origin to China under 102.11(b)(1).

key_factors: (b) essential character of the Chinese valve blanks

reasoning: Engine intake and exhaust valves are classified in heading 8409 (parts of engines of 8407/8408). In Mexico, grinding, turning, and chrome plating do not change the tariff classification from heading 8409, failing the 19 CFR 102.20 tariff shift under 102.11(a)(3). Under 102.11(b), the Chinese blanks impart the essential character.

key_factors: (b) essential character of the jumbo rolls of self-adhesive paper (4811.41) and polypropylene film (3919.90)
decisive_step: Manufacturing of the self-adhesive paper and polypropylene film jumbo rolls (coating and laminating with adhesive and release liner) in China
flip: Slitting the jumbo rolls in the intermediate country into rolls of a width not exceeding 15 cm (for paper under heading 4811) or 20 cm (for plastic film under heading 3919), or performing the adhesive coating and laminating there.
reasoning: Following exact precedent N341007 involving identical facts and products, jumbo rolls of self-adhesive paper (4811.41) and polypropylene labelstock (3919.90) produced in China are merely slit into narrower rolls of 10 to 22 inches (25.4 to 55.88 cm) in a third country (such as Canada or Mexico). Because the slit rolls exceed 15 cm (4811) and 20 cm (3919), they fail the 19 CFR 102.20 tariff shift under 102.11(a)(3). Under 102.11(b), the Chinese jumbo rolls impart the essential character.

key_factors: (a)(3) tariff shift to 8471.70
decisive_step: Assembly and interconnection of the magnetic tape storage modules and cabinet into a storage unit of subheading 8471.70 in Mexico
flip: If the individual storage modules were already classified as complete storage units of subheading 8471.70 when imported into Mexico, they would fail the 102.20 tariff shift rule (which requires a shift from any other subheading) and origin would revert under 102.11(b) or (d) to the country of origin of the modules.
reasoning: The Serverless Rack functions as a mass magnetic tape data storage unit meeting Chapter 84 Note 6(C), classified under subheading 8471.70, HTSUS. Assembling the metal cabinet, parts, and subassemblies (8473) into the interconnected 8471.70 storage unit at BDT de México's facility in Mexico satisfies the tariff shift under 19 CFR 102.11(a)(3), conferring Mexican origin.

key_factors: (a)(3) tariff shift to heading 7007 (or 8708.22)
decisive_step: Heating, bending, annealing, laminating the flat glass, and assembling with sensors and brackets in Mexico
flip: Importing the glass into Mexico already bent and laminated to the shape of the windshield from China, leaving only sensor/bracket attachment in Mexico.
reasoning: The finished automotive windshield is classified in heading 7007 (laminated safety glass of size and shape suitable for incorporation in vehicles) or subheading 8708.22. Under 19 CFR 102.20, the foreign materials undergo the required change in tariff classification from other headings to heading 7007 (or 8708.22). Thus, under 19 CFR 102.11(a)(3), the country of origin is Mexico.

key_factors: (b) essential character of the raw steel forgings
decisive_step: Heating, forging, and heat-treating steel billets into rough forgings in the shape of flanges and fittings in China (or Italy or India, respectively)
flip: Import raw steel billets of heading 7207 into Mexico and perform the forging and heat-treating operations in Mexico so the tariff shift to heading 7307 occurs there.
reasoning: The finished steel flanges, crosses, and tees are classified in heading 7307. Under 19 CFR 102.20, heading 7307 requires a change from any other heading. The imported rough forgings from China, Italy, or India already have the approximate shape of the finished goods and are classified in heading 7307 under GRI 2(a) (or as rough forgings of 7307). Because they do not undergo a tariff shift in Mexico under 102.11(a)(3), 102.11(b) applies, and the single material (the forging) imparts the essential character.

key_factors: (b)(1) essential character of the bicycle frame
decisive_step: Manufacturing of the bicycle frame (classified in heading 8714) in Taiwan
flip: Manufacture the bicycle frame in Canada so that all foreign components of heading 8714 either are eliminated or the frame is domestic, or manufacture the frame in China.
reasoning: The Katahdin bicycle is classified in heading 8712. The 19 CFR 102.20 tariff shift rule for heading 8712 requires a change from any other heading, except from heading 8714. Because the imported frame, brakes, wheels, and saddle are classified in heading 8714, they fail the shift under 102.11(a)(3). Under 102.11(b)(1) and 102.18(b), and consistent with N295820, the bicycle frame imparts the essential character of the bicycle. Assuming the frame originates in Taiwan, the country of origin is Taiwan.

key_factors: (b)(1) essential character of the single foreign material (nickel powder) that did not undergo the required tariff shift
decisive_step: Manufacturing of the pure nickel powder by hydrometallurgy in Australia
flip: Importing the nickel into Canada as unwrought nickel (heading 7502) or nickel mattes/sinters (heading 7501) and converting it into powder (heading 7504) in Canada, satisfying the 102.20 tariff shift.
reasoning: The good is classified under heading 7504. It is not wholly obtained or produced exclusively from domestic materials in Canada under 102.11(a)(1)-(2). Under 102.11(a)(3), the 102.20 rule for 7504 requires a change from any other heading. Because the Australian input is already nickel powder of heading 7504, screening, cutting, and packaging in Canada do not cause a tariff shift. Under 102.11(b)(1), the single material imparting the essential character is the Australian nickel powder, making the origin Australia.

key_factors: (b)(1) essential character of the nonalloy steel coil
decisive_step: Melting, pouring, and manufacturing the flat-rolled nonalloy steel coils in Brazil
flip: Cold-forming the coils in Mexico from hot-rolled steel coils of heading 7208 instead of coated flat-rolled steel of heading 7210/7212, or further preparing the sheets into identifiable structural roofing parts of heading 7308 in Mexico.
reasoning: The roll-formed angular profile sheets are classified in heading 7216 (specifically subheading 7216.91). For goods of 7216.61 through 7216.99, the 19 CFR 102.20 tariff shift rule requires a change from any other heading, except from headings 7208 through 7215. Because the Brazilian coils of 7210/7212 fail the tariff shift under 102.11(a)(3), 102.11(b)(1) applies. The single foreign material (the steel coil) imparts the essential character, making Brazil the origin.

key_factors: (a)(3) tariff shift to subheading 8507.90
decisive_step: Forming the steel into the cylindrical battery can and assembling it with the rivet and gasket in Mexico
flip: Importing the steel can already stamped/formed into a recognizable battery part (8507.90) from South Korea, so the tariff shift fails in Mexico.
reasoning: The finished 4680 Cylindrical Can Assembly is classified under subheading 8507.90.8000, HTSUS. The 19 CFR 102.20 tariff shift rule for subheading 8507.90 requires a change to subheading 8507.90 from any other subheading. The Korean-origin raw steel (Chapter 72), rivet (Chapter 73/83), and gasket (Chapter 39/40) are classified outside subheading 8507.90. When the steel is formed into a battery can and assembled with the rivet and gasket in Mexico, all foreign materials undergo the required tariff shift under 19 CFR 102.11(a)(3).

key_factors: (a)(3) tariff shift to heading 8708
decisive_step: Permanent press-fitting assembly of the Taiwanese oil seal and Indian bearing cone in Mexico (under the USMCA/Part 102 scenario)
flip: If the assembly were classified in subheading 8482.20 as a tapered roller bearing cone rather than a motor vehicle part of heading 8708, the Indian bearing cone (8482.20 or 8482.99) would fail the 102.20 tariff shift in Mexico, shifting origin to India under 102.11(b).
reasoning: Because the rubber oil seal adds significant non-friction-reducing capabilities, the assembly is excluded from heading 8482 and classified as a motor vehicle part under heading 8708 (8708.99). Under 19 CFR 102.11(a)(3), the 102.20 rule for 8708.99 requires a change from any other heading (or subheading). In the Mexico scenario (where Part 102 applies for marking), the Taiwanese oil seal (4016) and Indian bearing cone (8482) both undergo the required tariff shift to heading 8708 when permanently press-fitted together in Mexico.

key_factors: (a)(3) tariff shift to subheading 8414.30
decisive_step: Manufacturing the stator and rotor and assembling the hermetic compressor from parts of 8414.90 and other materials in Mexico
flip: Importing the compressor as an unassembled kit of finished subassemblies (including pre-made stator, rotor, and pump assembly) from China that already has the essential character of a complete compressor under GRI 2(a)
reasoning: The hermetic compressors are classified in subheading 8414.30, HTSUS. Under 19 CFR 102.20(o), the tariff shift rule for 8414.10-8414.80 requires a change from any other subheading, including another subheading within that group. The foreign components—including compressor parts of subheading 8414.90, raw laminations, enameled wire, and aluminum ingot—are manufactured into the stator and rotor and assembled into the finished compressor in Mexico. Because all foreign materials undergo the required tariff shift in Mexico, origin is Mexico under 19 CFR 102.11(a)(3) (consistent with H315287 and H318255).

key_factors: (a)(3) tariff shift to heading 2106 (or 1905)
decisive_step: Preparation, assembly, wrapping, and freezing of the breakfast wraps in Canada
flip: Perform the assembly and preparation of the wraps in the United States using the same ingredients
reasoning: The frozen breakfast sandwich wrap is a food preparation classified in heading 2106 (or 1905). It is not wholly obtained (102.11(a)(1)) or made exclusively from domestic materials (102.11(a)(2)). Under 19 CFR 102.11(a)(3), the applicable 102.20 tariff shift rule for heading 2106 (or 1905) requires a change from any other heading (or chapter). All foreign ingredients (lavash of 1905 if finished is 2106, eggs, vegetables, spices, etc.) undergo the required tariff shift when prepared and assembled into wraps in Canada.

key_factors: (b)(1) essential character of the thermoplastic vulcanizate (TPV) / propylene copolymer
decisive_step: Production of the base thermoplastic vulcanizate (TPV) / propylene copolymer in Japan
flip: Produce the base TPV / propylene copolymer in Mexico (or perform the polymerization from monomers classified in Chapter 29 in Mexico) so that all foreign inputs undergo the required tariff shift under 19 CFR 102.20.
reasoning: The finished propylene elastomer pellets are classified in subheading 3902.30.00. For goods processed in Mexico, 19 CFR 102.20 requires a change to headings 3901-3915 from any other heading (with conditions inside Ch. 39). The Japanese base TPV/propylene polymers are already classified in heading 3902, failing the tariff shift under 102.11(a)(3) through simple melting, blending, and pelletizing. Under 102.11(b)(1), the Japanese TPV (~63.5% by weight, providing the base thermoplastic properties) imparts the essential character, making Japan the country of origin.

key_factors: (a)(3) tariff shift to subheading 9401.39

decisive_step: Processing the raw stainless steel hypo-tube and constantan wire into a thermocouple subassembly and assembling the complete RF probe in Mexico
flip: Importing the thermocouple subassembly or an unfinished RF probe already classified in subheading 9018.90 into Mexico for mere attachment of the handle and cable
reasoning: The finished radio frequency (RF) ablation probe is an electrosurgical instrument or part thereof classified under subheading 9018.90, HTSUS (rather than 9018.39). The 19 CFR 102.20 tariff shift rule for 9018.90 requires a change from any other subheading. All foreign materials imported into Mexico—including the stainless steel hypo-tubes (Chapter 73), insulated constantan wire and three-conductor cable (heading 8544), four-pin connector (heading 8536), and plastic sheath (Chapter 39)—are classified outside subheading 9018.90 and undergo the required tariff shift in Mexico under 19 CFR 102.11(a)(3).
